statement: (i) Use the quotient rule to differentiate $y=\frac{\ln x}{x}$ for $x>0$. (ii) Find the x-coordinate of its stationary point and determine its nature. (iii) Show that $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{\ln x}{x}=0$.
solution: (i) $y'=\frac{(1/x)\cdot x-\ln x\cdot 1}{x^{2}}=\frac{1-\ln x}{x^{2}}$. (ii) Stationary where $1-\ln x=0\Rightarrow x=e$. For $x<e$, $y'>0$; for $x>e$, $y'<0$, so it is a maximum. (iii) As $x\to\infty$, $\ln x$ grows slower than any positive power of $x$; by L'Hopital, $\lim\frac{\ln x}{x}=\lim\frac{1/x}{1}=0$.
hints: Use L'Hopital or growth comparison for the limit.
